raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen2.5-VL video embeddings are wrong: full-attention `cu_seqlens` treats the whole video as one segment, while  HF and vLLM use one segment per frame (as already fixed for Qwen3-VL in #11458).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_5_vl.py`:
- `forward`: `cu_seqlens` per temporal step, `repeat_interleave(h*w, t).cumsum()` instead of `(t*h*w).cumsum()`.
- `forward_with_cuda_graph`: same change.
- `forward_with_cuda_graph`: build the `full_layout` graph key per temporal step, so it matches `cu_seqlens`.

Images (t=1) are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, 36 MVBench video clips, bf16, NVIDIA A10, sglang 0.5.22 (vision code identical to main).
Vision embeddings compared with HF transformers' encoder in fp32 on identical pixels (median cosine per clip):

| | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| HF bf16 (noise floor) | 0.9941 | 0.9991 | 0.9997 |
| before | 0.5929 | 0.8912 | 0.9692 |
| after | 0.9939 | 0.9991 | 0.9997 |

- After the fix, every clip is within HF's own bf16 noise.
- 7/36 answers change; accuracy is 58.3% before and after.
- With `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, outputs are identical to eager (cosine 1.0000) before and after the change.
- Unrelated to this change: with the ViT CUDA graph, the server ran out of memory after ~30 distinct video shapes on a 24 GB GPU, both before and after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The change makes the full-attention segments smaller (per temporal step instead of per video), so it does not add attention work.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Related: #11458 (same fix for Qwen3-VL), #12261 (earlier Qwen2.5-VL attempt, closed by the stale bot)

@@ -546,10 +546,11 @@ def forward(
         )
 
         # compute cu_seqlens - move cu_seqlens to GPU and make it int32
+        # one full-attention segment per temporal step (h * w tokens), as in HF
         cu_seqlens = torch.cat(
             [
                 torch.tensor([0], device=x.device, dtype=torch.int32),
-                (grid_thw[:, 0] * grid_thw[:, 1] * grid_thw[:, 2])
+                torch.repeat_interleave(grid_thw[:, 1] * grid_thw[:, 2], grid_thw[:, 0])
                 .cumsum(dim=0)
                 .to(device=x.device, dtype=torch.int32),
             ]
@@ -642,20 +643,23 @@ def forward_with_cuda_graph(
         )
 
         # compute cu_seqlens - move cu_seqlens to GPU and make it int32
+        # one full-attention segment per temporal step (h * w tokens), as in HF
         cu_seqlens = torch.cat(
             [
                 torch.tensor([0], device=x.device, dtype=torch.int32),
-                (grid_thw[:, 0] * grid_thw[:, 1] * grid_thw[:, 2])
+                torch.repeat_interleave(grid_thw[:, 1] * grid_thw[:, 2], grid_thw[:, 0])
                 .cumsum(dim=0)
                 .to(device=x.device, dtype=torch.int32),
             ]
         )
         cu_seqlens = torch.cat([cu_seqlens.new_zeros(1), cu_seqlens])
+        # graph key: must match the cu_seqlens boundaries above
         full_layout = [0, 0]
         total_tokens = 0
         for temporal, height, width in grid_thw.tolist():
-            total_tokens += temporal * height * width
-            full_layout.append(total_tokens)
+            for _ in range(temporal):
+                total_tokens += height * width
+                full_layout.append(total_tokens)
 
         return self.cuda_graph_runner.run(
             x=x,
